# **CalSnap Clone — Use Case Specification & Business Logic**

## **Graduation Thesis (Đồ án tốt nghiệp) — MVP Scope · Version 3.0 (Consolidated)**

Table of Contents

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**About this version.** v1.0 was written from the ERD and the feature-survey document. v2.0 revised it against a screen recording of the real published CalSnap app, but was written as a *delta* — it referred back to v1 for unchanged material and was therefore not usable on its own. **This version merges both into a single self-contained specification.** Nothing is referenced externally; every formula, flow and business rule appears in full below.

**Provenance markers** used throughout, so the origin of each claim stays auditable in your thesis: **\[Confirmed\]** — verified against the real app’s observed UI · **\[Updated\]** — revised because of an observation · **\[Assumption\]** — this document’s own design proposal, not observed and not sourced · **\[Stretch\]** / **\[Out of scope\]** — deliberate MVP scope decisions (see §6).

---

## **0\. Actors**

| Actor | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Guest** | Unauthenticated visitor; can only Register/Login. |
| **User** | Authenticated end-user. Single tier for the MVP — no Free/Premium gating is required, though subscription\_tier exists in the schema for future use. |
| **System (Scheduler)** | Secondary/background actor — triggers automatic jobs: daily goal snapshot creation, day-boundary rollover, streak/challenge reset. Not a human actor, but must be modelled because several use cases are system-initiated rather than user-initiated. |
| **AI / NLP Service** *\[Stretch\]* | Third-party vision API for photo recognition (UC-15a) and text-parsing API for free-text “Type” logging (UC-15b). **\[Confirmed\]** both exist in the real app; both remain stretch-only here. |
| **Third-Party Health Service** *\[Out of scope\]* | Apple Health / Google Fit — source for ACTIVITY\_LOG.source. |

## **2\. Use Cases by Module**

### **Module A — Authentication & Account**

#### *UC-01 — Register Account*

* **Actor:** Guest

* **Trigger:** User taps “Sign up” / “Get started”

* **Precondition:** Email not already registered

* **Main Flow:**

  1. Guest enters email \+ password (or OAuth).

  2. System validates email format and password strength.

  3. System creates a USER row — only id, email, password\_hash, created\_at populated; all profile fields NULL until onboarding.

  4. System creates a session/token and redirects to Onboarding (UC-05).

* **Business Rules:**

  * Password must be hashed (bcrypt/argon2), never stored in plaintext.

  * The USER row exists *before* onboarding completes, so profile fields must be nullable until UC-05 finishes. This lets a user who abandons onboarding resume later, and avoids an incomplete-signup dead state.

  * No DAILY\_GOAL exists at this point, so the dashboard must handle a “goal not yet computed” state defensively (UC-09 edge cases).

#### *UC-02 — Login*

* **Actor:** Guest → User

* **Trigger:** User submits credentials

* **Main Flow:**

  1. Validate credentials.

  2. Issue session token.

  3. Route conditionally: if a DAILY\_GOAL exists → Dashboard; otherwise → resume Onboarding.

* **Business Rule:** Login routing depends on onboarding completion, not merely on authentication success.

#### *UC-03 — Logout*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** Invalidate session/token → clear local cache → return to Login screen.

#### *UC-04 — Edit Profile*

* **Actor:** User

* **Trigger:** User opens Settings and edits gender / birth\_year / height / weight\_current / weight\_goal / activity\_level / unit\_system / diet\_type / calorie\_calc\_mode

* **Main Flow:**

  1. User changes one or more profile fields.

  2. System validates input ranges (§3.7).

  3. System persists the change to USER.

  4. **«include» UC-08** — System recalculates and snapshots a new DAILY\_GOAL.

* **Business Rules:**

  * Any field feeding the BMR/TDEE formula (gender, birth\_year, height, weight\_current, activity\_level, weight\_goal) triggers recalculation. Editing only email/password does not.

  * Editing weight\_current here versus logging via UC-18 is a **duplication risk** — see Q9.

* **\[Updated\]** The real app splits profile editing across **two surfaces**: “Personal details” under an Account section, and a separate **Customization** section holding unit\_system, appearance and language. For the MVP, keep these unified in one screen unless you want to mirror the split for realism (§5, item 8).

---

### **Module B — Onboarding**

#### *UC-05 — Complete Onboarding Flow*

* **Actor:** User (post-registration, first session)

* **Trigger:** Automatic redirect after UC-01, or resumed from Login

* **Precondition:** DAILY\_GOAL does not yet exist for this user

* **Main Flow** — **\[Updated\]** re-sequenced to match the observed screen order:

  1. Select gender (Female / Male / Prefer not to answer).

  2. Select birth year (scroll picker).

  3. **\[Confirmed, new\]** Notification permission screen — headed **“Stay on track”**, listing Meal time reminders, Progress tracking alerts, Motivational check-ins, and Water reminders, with a toggle to enable or skip. Non-blocking: it must not gate progression.

  4. Select unit system — **\[Confirmed\]** exact copy is **“What’s your units?”** — Metric (m, kg, ml) / Imperial (ft, lbs, fl oz), single-select. A progress bar runs across the whole flow, confirming onboarding is a fixed, numbered sequence.

  5. Enter height (picker; unit per step 4).

  6. Enter current weight (picker, decimal allowed).

  7. Select activity level (Sedentary → Extremely active).

  8. **\[Updated\]** Select weight goal — **\[Confirmed\]** exact copy is **“What is your weight goal?”** — exactly three radio options: Lose weight / Maintain weight / Gain weight. This is a **separate step** from the rate slider; v1 incorrectly conflated the two.

  9. **If** goal ≠ Maintain → separate rate-slider step (turtle↔rabbit) → system computes weight\_goal and target date, and warns if the rate falls outside the safe range (§3.3). *\[Assumption — this step was not directly re-observed in the recording; it is carried forward from v1 and is unverified rather than confirmed.\]*

  10. **If** goal \= Maintain → weight\_goal \= weight\_current.

  11. **\[Confirmed, new\]** “Creating your plan… / Finalizing results…” loading screen with a 0→100% progress ring. Goal calculation is presented to the user as an explicit async step. This is a UX pattern, not evidence about the underlying data model.

  12. **«include» UC-07** — System computes BMR → TDEE → target kcal → macro grams → creates the first DAILY\_GOAL row with effective\_date \= today.

  13. Results screen: calorie ring, macro breakdown, BMI gauge (Underweight/Healthy/Overweight/Obese), projected goal date.

  14. User confirms → routed to Dashboard (UC-09).

* **Business Rules:**

  * All six core fields (gender, birth\_year, height, weight\_current, activity\_level, goal) are **mandatory** before UC-07 can run — partial data cannot produce a DAILY\_GOAL.

  * diet\_type and calorie\_calc\_mode are collected in the full CalSnap flow but are not in the stated MVP mandatory list. If you drop those screens, default diet\_type \= "Balanced" and calorie\_calc\_mode \= "Smart mode" rather than leaving them NULL — both are read by the UC-07 and UC-11 formulas.

---

### **Module C — Goal Calculation *(system-driven; no user-facing screens)***

#### *UC-07 — Calculate BMR / TDEE / Daily Goal*

* **Actor:** System (invoked by UC-05 or UC-08)

* **Trigger:** Onboarding completion, or a triggering profile edit

* **Main Flow** — full formulas in §3:

  1. Compute BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor, sex-specific) — §3.1.

  2. Compute TDEE \= BMR × activity multiplier — §3.2.

  3. Apply goal adjustment (deficit/surplus) with safe-rate clamping → target\_kcal — §3.3.

  4. Apply macro % split from diet\_type → target\_carbs\_g, target\_protein\_g, target\_fat\_g — §3.4.

  5. Set target\_water\_ml (default 2000 ml — **\[Confirmed\]** as the real app’s default).

  6. Insert a new DAILY\_GOAL row with effective\_date \= today.

* **Output:** one DAILY\_GOAL row.

#### *UC-08 — Recalculate Daily Goal on Profile Change*

* **Actor:** System (invoked by UC-04; by UC-25 if calc-mode changes are treated as formula-relevant; and by UC-18 if you choose to auto-sync weight\_current from the latest WEIGHT\_LOG)

* **Main Flow:** Identical computation to UC-07, except that it **inserts a new row** with effective\_date \= today rather than creating the first one. It does **not** UPDATE the previous row — see the snapshot rationale in §3.5.

* **Business Rule:** Past days continue to resolve to whichever DAILY\_GOAL row has the most recent effective\_date ≤ that day.

---

### **Module D — Dashboard**

#### *UC-09 — View Daily Dashboard*

* **Actor:** User

* **Trigger:** App open / navigate to Home

* **Main Flow:**

  1. System resolves “today” in the user’s local time (§3.8).

  2. System fetches the DAILY\_GOAL row effective for today (§3.5).

  3. System aggregates for that day: SUM(FOOD\_ENTRY.total\_kcal); SUM(carbs\_g / protein\_g / fat\_g); SUM(ACTIVITY\_LOG.calories\_burned); SUM(WATER\_LOG.amount\_ml); and the latest WEIGHT\_LOG.weight.

  4. System renders Target/Consumed/Burned kcal, macro progress bars, water grid, and weight-versus-goal delta.

  5. **«include» UC-11** for the calories-left computation.

  6. **«include» UC-18** — **\[Updated\]** weight can be logged inline from the dashboard card without navigating away.

* **\[Confirmed\] Header contents:** app logo, **week-day selector** (Mon–Sun, current day highlighted), **coin-balance indicator**, **settings gear icon**. Day selection and the gamification currency both live on the main dashboard rather than on separate screens.

* **\[Confirmed\] Card behaviours:**

  * **Water card** shows the goal numerically (“Goal: 2 000 ml”) and carries a **“…” overflow menu**, implying per-card edit/delete actions rather than passive display. Apply this pattern consistently across cards.

  * **Weight card** shows current weight with the delta phrased on one line as **“X kg above/below goal: \<goal\_value\>”**, plus an inline **“+” quick-add**.

  * **Calories cards** — “Calories left” as a large number with a small progress ring and a thumbnail of the last logged meal; “Calories burned” with a “No activities yet” empty state.

* **Edge cases (empty states):**

  * No DAILY\_GOAL yet → block the dashboard and force-redirect to onboarding. Should not occur after UC-05, but must be handled defensively.

  * No FOOD\_ENTRY today → Consumed \= 0, macro bars at 0%.

  * No ACTIVITY\_LOG today → Burned \= 0, display “No activities yet”.

  * No WATER\_LOG today → 0/target, empty cup grid.

  * No WEIGHT\_LOG ever → show weight\_current from onboarding with no trend, or an explicit “Log your first weigh-in” prompt.

#### *UC-10 — Select Day (Week Selector)*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** User taps a day (Mon–Sun) other than today → System re-runs UC-09’s aggregation scoped to that date, and resolves the DAILY\_GOAL **effective as of that date** — not necessarily today’s goal (§3.5).

* **Business Rule:** Future dates should be disabled, or shown with an all-zero empty state, since no logs can exist yet.

#### *UC-11 — View / Compute Calories Left & Burned*

* **Actor:** System (included by UC-09, UC-12, UC-13, UC-14, UC-16)

* **Main Flow:** Exact formula in §3.6. Recomputed synchronously on every insert, update or delete affecting FOOD\_ENTRY or ACTIVITY\_LOG for the day in question — aggregation at query time, not a stored running counter (rationale in §3.6).

---

### **Module E — Food Logging**

**\[Confirmed\] Four input methods**, presented as a segmented tab control: **Voice · Image · Type · Manual**. v1 modelled only manual and photo. Scope treatment of each is in §6.

#### *UC-12 — Log Food Manually (MVP core)*

* **Actor:** User

* **Trigger:** Tap “+” → Food, or the MANUAL tab in the entry screen

* **Main Flow:**

  1. User enters — **\[Confirmed\]** exact field order: **Meal name** → **Amount eaten toggle (Grams vs Serving)** → **Calories** → **Macronutrients** section (Carbs, Protein, Fat). **\[Confirmed\]** each numeric field uses a **“+” stepper-style input**, not a bare numeric field.

  2. System validates numeric ranges (§3.7) and optionally checks kcal-versus-macro consistency (§3.7).

  3. System inserts FOOD\_ENTRY with input\_method \= "manual" and logged\_at \= now().

  4. **«include» UC-11** — dashboard totals refresh.

  5. **\[Updated\]** **«include» UC-22** — a post-log challenge interstitial may appear (gamification; out of MVP core).

* **Business Rules:**

  * logged\_at determines which calendar day (in the user’s local time) the entry counts toward — critical for the midnight edge case (§3.8).

  * **\[Confirmed — resolves Q10\]** The manual entry screen has **no ingredient list**. Ingredient breakdown appears only on the AI result screen (UC-15a). Manual entry is therefore **aggregate-only**, and **FOOD\_ENTRY requires its own name column** — do not rely on INGREDIENT.name, since no INGREDIENT rows are created in this flow.

  * **New validation requirement:** if “Serving” is selected on the amount toggle, the system needs a serving-size→grams reference to convert for storage. No such reference was observed — see Q12.

#### *UC-13 — Edit Food Entry (MVP core)*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** Open an existing FOOD\_ENTRY → edit fields → save → **«include» UC-11**.

* **Business Rule:** Editing does **not** change logged\_at unless the user explicitly changes the date/time. The entry stays attributed to its original day.

#### *UC-14 — Delete Food Entry (MVP core)*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** Delete the FOOD\_ENTRY, cascading to its child INGREDIENT rows → **«include» UC-11**.

#### *UC-15a — Log Food via AI Photo Recognition \[Stretch\]*

* **Actor:** User, AI/NLP Service

* **Main Flow:**

  1. **\[Confirmed, new\]** Pre-capture coaching screen — headed **“Before moving”** — shows a side-by-side Good-photo versus Bad-photo example, with an on-camera framing guide instructing that food be placed inside the auxiliary box. A deliberate step to raise recognition accuracy.

  2. Capture or select a photo.

  3. Send to a third-party vision API (Nutritionix / LogMeal / OpenAI Vision) rather than training a model.

  4. Parse the response into a draft FOOD\_ENTRY plus child INGREDIENT rows.

  5. **\[Confirmed\]** Result screen shows food name, weight in grams, total kcal and macro breakdown, plus an **Ingredients** section itemising recognised components (e.g. “Pepperoni Pizza — 650g — 1730 kcal” with per-ingredient macro indicators) and an **“Add new ingredient”** action.

  6. User reviews and adjusts, then confirms save (as UC-12 from step 3 onward).

* **Business Rules:**

  * input\_method \= "image"; ai\_feedback starts NULL.

  * **\[Confirmed\]** A thumbs-up/down control headed **“How did CalSnap do?”** sits directly on the result screen and writes to FOOD\_ENTRY.ai\_feedback.

  * **\[Confirmed\]** **Fiber level** is present but **paywall-locked** (lock icon \+ “View your fiber intake” CTA) on both this screen and the dashboard. Fiber exists in the real data model and is Premium-gated, not simply unbuilt. Keep FOOD\_ENTRY.fiber\_g in the schema as a nullable, unused column; build no paywall logic for the MVP.

  * Recognition failure must fall back gracefully to manual entry.

#### *UC-15b — Log Food via Type (Free-Text / NLP) \[Stretch\]*

* **Actor:** User, AI/NLP Service

* **Trigger:** User selects the “Type” tab

* **Main Flow:** **\[Confirmed\]** User types a free-text description into a box prompting *“Type what you ate (e.g., 2 eggs, a slice of bread, 1 avocado)”* → System sends the text to an NLP/parsing service → service returns structured items with estimated kcal/macros → user reviews and confirms → FOOD\_ENTRY created with input\_method \= "type".

* **Scope note:** A distinct third AI-assisted input method, absent from v1 entirely. Same complexity class as UC-15a.

#### *UC-15c — Log Food via Voice \[Out of scope\]*

* **\[Confirmed\]** present as the fourth tab in the real app. No speech-to-text integration is planned. Either omit the Voice tab from your clone’s UI or render it disabled, so the segmented control doesn’t imply a feature that doesn’t exist.

### **Module F — Activity Logging *(needed to support “Burned” on the dashboard)***

#### *UC-16 — Log Activity Manually / via Preset*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow** — **\[Updated\]**, the real screen offers two paths:

  1. **Preset list *(MVP-recommended path)*** — **\[Confirmed\]** a list of activity types with kcal-burn already computed per 30 minutes (Walking 141 kcal/30min, Running 351, Cycling 324, Elliptical, …), each with a one-tap “+” and a **time picker** for when the activity happened. Implement as a static lookup table: calories\_burned \= rate × (duration\_minutes / 30\). No AI needed.

  2. **Free-text *\[Stretch\]*** — **\[Confirmed\]** *“Type your workout (e.g., cycling for 45 minutes)”*, which is another NLP-assisted parse in the same complexity class as UC-15b.

  3. Insert ACTIVITY\_LOG with source \= "manual" → **«include» UC-11** → **«include» UC-22**.

* **Business Rule:** **\[Updated\]** The time picker means ACTIVITY\_LOG.logged\_at can be **backdated** independently of insertion time. All day-bucketing logic (§3.6, §3.8) must key off logged\_at/recorded\_at, never off the moment the row was written.

#### *UC-17 — Sync Activity from Health App \[Out of scope\]*

* **Actor:** User, Apple Health / Google Fit — imports ACTIVITY\_LOG rows with source \= "apple\_health" / "google\_fit". Not observed in the recording; requires platform-specific SDK work disproportionate to MVP value.

---

### **Module G — Weight Tracking**

#### *UC-18 — Log Weight*

* **Actor:** User

* **Trigger:** **\[Confirmed\]** the “+” directly on the dashboard Weight card, or the Quick-add sheet. Most commonly triggered from UC-09 rather than from a dedicated screen.

* **Main Flow:** Enter weight (decimal, in the user’s unit system) → convert to canonical storage unit (§3.7 / Q1) → insert WEIGHT\_LOG with recorded\_at \= today → **«include» UC-19** to refresh the trend → optionally prompt to update USER.weight\_current.

* **Business Rules:**

  * If more than one WEIGHT\_LOG exists for the same recorded\_at date, “current weight” should resolve to the **most recently created** row for that date.

  * **\[Updated\]** Because logging and current-weight display share one card, the two concepts are presented to the user as unified — suggestive evidence for Q9, though not proof about the backend.

#### *UC-19 — View Weight History / Trend*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** Fetch all WEIGHT\_LOG rows for the user ordered by recorded\_at → render as a line chart → compute delta \= latest\_weight − USER.weight\_goal → display as “X kg above/below goal: \<goal\_value\>”.

* **Edge case:** Zero logs → render weight\_current from onboarding as a single point, or show an empty-chart call to action. A single data point must not crash the chart.

---

### **Module H — Water Tracking**

#### *UC-20 — Log Water Intake*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** Tap “+” on the Water card for a fixed increment (e.g. 250 ml), or enter a custom amount → insert WATER\_LOG with logged\_at \= now() → **«include» UC-21** → **«include» UC-22**.

* **\[Updated\]** The card also carries a **“…” overflow menu**, so the use case includes an edit/delete path, not only the “+” tap.

#### *UC-21 — View Water Progress*

* **Actor:** User (included by UC-09)

* **Main Flow:** SUM(WATER\_LOG.amount\_ml) for the selected day ÷ DAILY\_GOAL.target\_water\_ml → render the cup grid / progress ring with the goal shown numerically.

### **Module I — Gamification *\[Out of MVP core — nice-to-have, lowest priority\]***

v1 listed these as schema placeholders. The recording shows them **fully built and central** to the real product, so they are specified here — while remaining explicitly deprioritised (§6).

#### *UC-22 — Post-Log Challenge Interstitial*

* **Actor:** System (triggered after UC-12, UC-16 or UC-20 completes)

* **Main Flow:** **\[Confirmed\]** A **“That’s tasty progress\!”** interstitial appears immediately after logging, showing three live challenge progress bars, each with a coin reward. Observed examples:

  * “Stay consistent — Log meals 3 times today — 1/3”

  * “Calorie balance — Reach 90% of your calorie goal — 1726/2284”

  * “Keep the streak — Stay active 5 days this week — 1/5”

  * Actions: **“Continue”** and **“Hide challenge progress”** (a per-user opt-out preference).

* **Schema mapping:** each bar is a QUEST row (progress / target / reward\_coins); “Calorie balance” reads live from UC-11’s aggregation; “Keep the streak” reads from STREAK.

#### *UC-23 — View Challenges Screen*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** **\[Confirmed\]** A **dedicated full screen** (not a modal) with **Daily** and **Weekly** sections. Each challenge shows a progress bar, a fraction (“0/5”), days remaining (“5d left”), and a coin reward.

#### *UC-24 — Award Coins on Quest Completion*

* **Actor:** System

* **Main Flow:** On quest completion, write a COIN\_TRANSACTION row and update the balance shown in the dashboard header. Feeds off the same QUEST / COIN\_TRANSACTION tables as UC-22 and UC-23.

#### *UC-24b — Update Streak*

* **Actor:** System — update STREAK on the first qualifying log of each day; reset current\_streak after a missed day while preserving longest\_streak. The real app also has a dedicated day-streak screen with a 7-day row, a share button and an “I’m committed” confirmation.

---

### **Module J — Settings & Preferences *(new module; not modelled in v1)***

#### *UC-25 — Edit Calorie-Calc Mode (“Smart mode”)*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** **\[Confirmed\]** Settings contains a field labelled exactly **“Smart mode”** next to “Burned calories”, with a pencil edit icon and a **“How it affects daily calories”** explainer link. This confirms the mode lives in Settings, not only in onboarding, and that the UI label maps directly onto USER.calorie\_calc\_mode.

* **Business Rule / open judgment call:** Changing this mode alters how calories\_left is computed (§3.6) but **not** target\_kcal itself. *\[Assumption\]* — recommend treating it as a **display-time setting only**, requiring no new DAILY\_GOAL snapshot row. Flag with your advisor if you’d rather version it.

* **Note:** the explainer link’s actual text was not captured, so the precise algorithmic definition of “Smart mode” remains unresolved (Q5).

#### *UC-26 — Edit Water / Step Goal Directly in Settings*

* **Actor:** User

* **Main Flow:** **\[Confirmed\]** Settings holds an independently editable **Step goal** and **Water goal (default 2000 ml)**, separate from the onboarding DAILY\_GOAL flow.

* **Business Rule:** **\[Updated\]** target\_water\_ml is confirmed to be user-editable **independently of the BMR/TDEE pipeline** — not everything in DAILY\_GOAL passes through UC-07/UC-08’s formula engine. *\[Assumption\]* — recommend that water-goal edits update the current DAILY\_GOAL row directly (or live in a separate USER.water\_goal\_ml field, bypassing versioning entirely) rather than triggering a full recompute. Step goal is **\[Out of scope\]**: the ERD has no step-count field.

#### *UC-27 — App Preferences \[Out of scope\]*

* **\[Confirmed\]** present: Appearance (Light/Dark/System), Language, “Begin again” (reset onboarding), Reminders, a “Challenge progress” visibility toggle, the Metric-system toggle, plus an anonymised account ID and social links. Cosmetic app-shell preferences with no bearing on core tracking logic; listed for completeness only.

## **3\. Business Logic & Formulas (Exact)**

Values marked *\[Assumption\]* are this document’s own reference figures, not lifted from the real app. **\[Updated\]** The real app’s Settings → **“Health information sources”** screen cites **USDA/HHS Dietary Guidelines 9th Ed., WHO Technical Report Series No. 916, Wadden et al. 2012 (Circulation), and Hall et al. 2012 (Am J Clin Nutr)**, behind an explicit medical disclaimer banner. That confirms *which* literature a nutrition app of this kind cites — it does not supply the specific numbers below. You still need to read those sources and extract the figures yourself, or state the tables as your own design simplification.

### **3.1 BMR — Mifflin-St Jeor Equation**

age \= current\_year \- USER.birth\_year   // approx., §3.9 / Q2

Male:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;BMR \= 10 × weight\_kg \+ 6.25 × height\_cm − 5 × age \+ 5

Female:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;BMR \= 10 × weight\_kg \+ 6.25 × height\_cm − 5 × age − 161

"Prefer not to answer":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;→ needs a defined rule (see Q11). Common approach:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;average the male/female formulas, i.e.  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BMR \= 10 × weight\_kg \+ 6.25 × height\_cm − 5 × age − 78  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;OR force the user to pick one for calculation only,  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;even if not displayed. Flagged — do not assume.

weight\_kg and height\_cm must be the **canonical metric values** regardless of unit\_system. Convert Imperial input to metric *before* applying this formula (§3.7 / Q1).

### **3.2 TDEE — Activity Multiplier Table**

TDEE \= BMR × activity\_multiplier

activity\_level            multiplier  
\-------------------------------------  
Sedentary                    1.2  
Lightly active               1.375  
Moderately active            1.55  
Very active                  1.725  
Extremely active             1.9

*\[Assumption\]* — the standard multiplier table paired with Mifflin-St Jeor. Confirm against whatever source your advisor requires.

### **3.3 Goal Adjustment — Deficit / Surplus with Safe-Rate Clamping**

1 kg body fat ≈ 7,700 kcal    \[Assumption — common approx.\]

weekly\_kcal\_adjustment \= desired\_kg\_per\_week × 7700  
daily\_kcal\_adjustment  \= weekly\_kcal\_adjustment / 7

if goal \== "Lose weight":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;target\_kcal \= TDEE − daily\_kcal\_adjustment  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;SAFE RANGE \[Assumption\]:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0.25 kg/week ≤ desired\_kg\_per\_week ≤ 1.0 kg/week  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;HARD FLOOR: target\_kcal must never fall below a  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;minimum safe intake, e.g. 1200 kcal (female) /  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;1500 kcal (male). Clamp, and warn the user if the  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;slider would push below this floor.

elif goal \== "Gain weight":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;target\_kcal \= TDEE \+ daily\_kcal\_adjustment  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;SAFE RANGE \[Assumption\]:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0.1 kg/week ≤ desired\_kg\_per\_week ≤ 0.5 kg/week

else:   \# "Maintain weight"  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;target\_kcal \= TDEE

weight\_goal and the projected goal date shown on the onboarding results screen:

kg\_to\_change   \= |weight\_current − weight\_goal|  
projected\_days \= kg\_to\_change / desired\_kg\_per\_week × 7  
projected\_date \= today \+ projected\_days

### **3.4 Macro Breakdown (grams from target\_kcal)**

kcal per gram:   carbs \= 4,   protein \= 4,   fat \= 9

% split by diet\_type   \[Assumption — reference splits, not  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;observed in the app\]:

diet\_type          carbs%   protein%   fat%  
\--------------------------------------------  
Balanced             40        30        30  
Low carb             25        35        40  
Low fat              55        25        20  
High protein         30        40        30  
Keto                  5        25        70  
Vegetarian           45        25        30   (see note)

Note: for Vegetarian the protein source differs; the % split is  
the same as Balanced.

target\_carbs\_g   \= (target\_kcal × carbs%)   / 4  
target\_protein\_g \= (target\_kcal × protein%) / 4  
target\_fat\_g     \= (target\_kcal × fat%)     / 9

Round grams to one decimal, and verify that re-multiplying the rounded grams back through the kcal-per-gram constants returns target\_kcal within tolerance.

### **3.5 DAILY\_GOAL Recalculation Strategy — Snapshot, Not Live**

*\[Assumption — this is a design recommendation, and one of the more consequential decisions in the project.\]*

DAILY\_GOAL should be an **append-only history table** keyed by effective\_date, not a single mutable row per user.

* On onboarding completion (UC-07) → insert row \#1 with effective\_date \= signup day.

* On any profile edit feeding the formula (UC-08) → insert a **new** row with effective\_date \= today. The previous row is left untouched.

* **Lookup rule** for any calendar day *D*: use the DAILY\_GOAL row with the **latest effective\_date that is ≤ D**.

* **Rationale:** this keeps historical targets honest. If a user switches from “lose 0.5 kg/week” to “maintain” on day 40, days 1–39 should still display the deficit target they were actually tracking against, rather than being silently rewritten.

**\[Updated\]** UC-26 confirms the real app treats DAILY\_GOAL as having at least two independently-updatable zones: kcal/macro targets driven by the formula engine, versus water/step targets edited directly by the user. The snapshot-versus-live question for the kcal/macro zone specifically remains open — Q3.

### **3.6 “Calories Left” and “Calories Burned” — Real-Time Computation**

consumed\_kcal \= SUM(FOOD\_ENTRY.total\_kcal)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;WHERE user\_id \= X AND day(logged\_at) \= D  
burned\_kcal   \= SUM(ACTIVITY\_LOG.calories\_burned)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;WHERE user\_id \= X AND day(logged\_at) \= D  
target\_kcal   \= DAILY\_GOAL.target\_kcal for day D   (§3.5)

if USER.calorie\_calc\_mode \== "Smart mode":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\# The activity\_level multiplier already bakes in typical daily  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\# activity, so only activity ABOVE the user's normal  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\# baseline should extend the budget. Simplest MVP  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\# reading: burned activity does NOT add back at all.  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;calories\_left \= target\_kcal − consumed\_kcal

elif USER.calorie\_calc\_mode \== "All calories":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\# Every logged activity adds back, athlete-style.  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;calories\_left \= target\_kcal − consumed\_kcal \+ burned\_kcal

*\[Assumption\]* — the “Smart mode” baseline is not defined in any source material. The interpretation above (the TDEE multiplier already includes routine activity, so Smart mode avoids double-counting) is the standard reading, but **\[Updated\]** the real app’s “How it affects daily calories” explainer was not captured in the recording. If you cannot obtain its wording, cite this in your thesis as *interpreted from the app’s explainer, not independently verified* (Q5).

Negative remaining calories should display as a real negative value rather than clamping to zero.

**Computation strategy:** aggregate with SUM() at read time — on dashboard load and after each mutating action — rather than maintaining a stored running-total column. This is simpler and avoids drift from a missed decrement on delete, and MVP data volumes make live aggregation cheap. Worth naming the trade-off in your thesis: at scale you would add caching or a materialised daily-summary table.

### **3.7 Input Validation & Unit Handling**

* **Canonical storage unit** *\[Assumption\]* — store height, weight\_current and weight\_goal always in **metric** (cm, kg) internally regardless of USER.unit\_system, converting only at the presentation layer. This keeps §3.1 unit-safe. The schema does not state this; confirm as a design decision (Q1).

* **Server-side range validation:** height 50–250 cm; weight 20–300 kg; birth\_year between (current\_year − 120\) and (current\_year − 10).

* **Macro-consistency check on manual entry** *\[Assumption\]* — abs(carbs\_g×4 \+ protein\_g×4 \+ fat\_g×9 − total\_kcal) ≤ tolerance (e.g. 10% or 50 kcal) → **warn, don’t hard-block**, since users round. Whether to enforce this at all is Q7.

* **\[Updated\] Serving conversion:** the **Grams vs Serving** toggle means that selecting “Serving” requires a serving-size→grams reference table. None was observed (Q12). For the MVP, grams-only is recommended.

* **\[Updated\] Stepper inputs** constrain values at the UI layer, which reduces invalid input independently of server-side validation.

### **3.8 Midnight / Timezone Day-Boundary**

* The ERD has **no timezone field** on USER, and **\[Updated\]** none was observed anywhere in the real app’s Settings (Language and Appearance were the only locale-adjacent settings). “Today” for aggregation in §3.6 must therefore be computed in *some* reference timezone that is currently undefined.

* *\[Assumption\]* — add USER.timezone (IANA string, e.g. Asia/Ho\_Chi\_Minh) captured from the device at signup, and bucket all logged\_at / recorded\_at timestamps into calendar days using it rather than server UTC midnight. Otherwise a user logging food at 11:45 PM local time may see it attributed to the wrong day.

* **\[Updated\]** UC-16’s time picker confirms at least one entity supports user-specified backdated timestamps. All day-bucketing must key off logged\_at / recorded\_at, never off row-insertion time.

* Accepting UTC-day bucketing is a legitimate MVP simplification **if stated explicitly as a known limitation** in the thesis (Q4).

### **3.9 Age Precision Gap**

USER stores only birth\_year, not a full birthdate, so age \= current\_year − birth\_year can be off by up to a year — someone born in December is treated as a year younger than they are for most of the year, relative to someone born in January. Mifflin-St Jeor moves by 5 kcal per year of age, so the effect is small but real. Either state it as a known simplification or capture full date of birth (Q2). **\[Updated\]** No full-DOB screen was observed; only the birth-year picker was reconfirmed.

## **4\. Open Questions — Status**

Twelve questions. One is resolved by observation, five are narrowed but not settled, five have no bearing from the observations, and one is new.

| \# | Question | Status | Evidence / Recommendation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Q1 | Store height/weight canonically in metric, or exactly as entered? | **STILL OPEN** | A storage-layer decision that UI observation cannot resolve. Recommend metric-canonical (§3.7). |
| Q2 | Is age ≈ current\_year − birth\_year acceptable, or capture full DOB? | **STILL OPEN** | Birth-year picker reconfirmed; no DOB screen observed. |
| Q3 | DAILY\_GOAL append-only snapshot history, or live recalculation? | **PARTIALLY INFORMED** | UC-26 shows water/step goals edited independently of the BMR/TDEE engine, so the table is not treated as one monolithic recompute. Whether target\_kcal/macros specifically use snapshots remains a genuine open decision. |
| Q4 | Add USER.timezone, or accept UTC-day bucketing? | **STILL OPEN** | No timezone setting observed anywhere in the app. |
| Q5 | What exactly is the “Smart mode” baseline? | **PARTIALLY INFORMED** | Label and Settings location confirmed exactly; the “How it affects daily calories” explainer text was not captured, so the algorithm is still an assumption. **A second recording opening that link would likely close this outright.** |
| Q6 | Macro % split per diet\_type — what to cite? | **PARTIALLY INFORMED** | The app’s “Health information sources” screen names USDA/HHS Dietary Guidelines 9th Ed. and WHO TRS 916\. The §3.4 table remains this document’s placeholder, not derived from those sources. |
| Q7 | Validate manual kcal against macros, or trust input? | **STILL OPEN** | Only the field layout was observed, no validation behaviour. |
| Q8 | What safe weight-change rate limits to enforce? | **PARTIALLY INFORMED** | Same citation screen names Wadden et al. 2012 and Hall et al. 2012, both directly on weight-loss energy balance. Specific kg/week thresholds still need extracting from those papers. |
| Q9 | Does UC-18 sync USER.weight\_current? | **PARTIALLY INFORMED** | The dashboard card unifies “display current weight” and “log new weight”, suggesting they’re one concept to the user — but this doesn’t prove a backend write-back. **Recommend** deriving current weight from the latest WEIGHT\_LOG at read time and treating USER.weight\_current as an onboarding baseline only: simpler, and it removes a whole class of sync bug. |
| Q10 | Ingredient breakdown in manual entry, or AI-only? | **RESOLVED** | Manual entry has no ingredient list; breakdown with “Add new ingredient” appears only on the AI result screen. **Decision: manual entry is aggregate-only; INGREDIENT is populated solely by UC-15a. Add a FOOD\_ENTRY.name column.** |
| Q11 | BMR formula for gender \= “Prefer not to answer”? | **STILL OPEN** | The observation covered the weight-goal screen, not downstream calculation behaviour. |
| Q12 | *(new)* What serving-size reference backs the Grams/Serving toggle? | **NEW / OPEN** | Toggle confirmed; no serving-size data observed. **Recommend grams-only for the MVP** unless you hand-build a small reference table — the effort-to-value ratio is poor. |

## **5\. Cheap UX Details Worth Replicating**

Low-effort, high-perceived-quality details from the real app. All are presentation-layer only, so they survive even after the AI features are cut.

1. **“Creating your plan…” loading ring** before the onboarding results screen. UC-07 is near-instant, but a 1.5–2 second progress animation makes the calculated plan feel substantial. Roughly 30 minutes of frontend work.

2. **Grams vs Serving toggle.** Even implementing grams-only (Q12), keep the toggle visible and disable “Serving” rather than removing the control — the form looks unfinished without it.

3. **“+”-stepper inputs** for Calories, Carbs, Protein and Fat instead of bare number fields. Trivial with a standard component, and it constrains input at the UI layer, which indirectly helps with Q7’s validation concern.

4. **Thumbs-up/down AI feedback control.** Even a no-op version that writes ai\_feedback and does nothing else costs almost nothing, and gives you something real to discuss about AI quality loops in your thesis.

5. **Exact one-line delta phrasing** — “X kg above/below goal: \<goal\>” on the Weight card, “Goal: \<value\>” on the Water card. Pure copywriting; makes the UI read as a finished product rather than a data dump.

6. **Per-card “…” overflow menu** across Calories, Water and Weight cards. One reusable component (Edit / View details / Delete today’s entries) applied consistently.

7. **Pre-capture photo coaching screen** (Good vs Bad example plus framing guide) — **only if you build UC-15a**. A cheap static screen that measurably improves real recognition accuracy.

8. **Two-surface settings split** (Account vs Customization) — optional polish, not a functional requirement. Keep UC-04 unified for the MVP.

---

## **6\. Explicit Scope Decisions**

Per the project’s stated priorities — manual entry required, AI photo optional, gamification and paywall lowest — the following confirmed real-app features are **deliberately excluded or deferred**, so their absence is documented rather than accidental.

| Feature (confirmed in the real app) | MVP status | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Voice input for food logging (UC-15c) | **Out of scope** | Needs speech-to-text plus NLP; adds nothing over Type mode for thesis purposes. |
| Type / free-text NLP food logging (UC-15b) | **Stretch** | Same complexity class as photo recognition; only if that is also in scope and time remains. |
| AI photo recognition \+ ingredient breakdown (UC-15a) | **Stretch** | Optional in the original scope. Use a third-party Vision API rather than training a model. |
| Pre-capture photo coaching screen | **Stretch, tied to UC-15a** | Only meaningful if photo recognition ships. |
| Fiber tracking (Premium-gated in the real app) | **Out of scope**; keep the schema column | No Premium tier planned. Keep FOOD\_ENTRY.fiber\_g nullable and unused; build no paywall logic. |
| Gamification: interstitial (UC-22), Challenges screen (UC-23), coins (UC-24), streak (UC-24b) | **Nice-to-have, lowest priority** | Confirmed central to the real product — it appears after every log — but explicitly deprioritised. Only after core tracking is complete and stable. |
| Premium paywall screens | **Out of scope** | No monetisation needed for a thesis MVP; SUBSCRIPTION stays schema-only. |
| Activity free-text NLP parsing | **Stretch** | Build the static preset-list path first (UC-16 core). |
| Health app sync — Apple Health / Google Fit (UC-17) | **Out of scope** | Platform-specific SDK work disproportionate to MVP value. |
| Step goal tracking | **Out of scope** | No step-count field exists in the ERD, and no step source is planned. |
| Appearance / Language / social links (UC-27) | **Out of scope** | Cosmetic app-shell preferences with no bearing on core logic. |
| Two-screen profile split | **Optional polish** | Keep UC-04 unified; the split is not a functional requirement. |

Changes to ERD v1.0.0 implied by the analysis above, collected for convenience:

| Change | Driver | Status |

| Add FOOD\_ENTRY.name | Manual entry captures a Meal name but creates no INGREDIENT rows | **Required** (Q10 resolved) |
| Add USER.timezone | Correct day-boundary bucketing (§3.8) | Recommended; Q4 open |
| Keep FOOD\_ENTRY.fiber\_g nullable/unused | Fiber is Premium-gated in the real app | Retain, do not implement |
| Confirm DAILY\_GOAL is append-only with effective\_date | Snapshot lookup rule (§3.5) | Design decision; Q3 open |
| Treat USER.weight\_current as an onboarding baseline only | Avoid duplication with WEIGHT\_LOG | Recommended; Q9 open |
| SUBSCRIPTION, STREAK, QUEST, COIN\_TRANSACTION remain schema-only | Gamification and Premium out of MVP core | Retain, do not implement |
